title: Kalyan Jewellers in red as report says mutual fund likely to sell around 5 crore shares- Moneycontrol.com
summary: Shares of Kalyan Jewellers fell after a report said a domestic mutual fund may offload about 5 crore shares in a block deal at an 8–10% discount. Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund holds roughly 9.17% (9.5 crore shares). The stock had rallied over 50% in a month; Citi maintains a Buy rating with a Rs 750 target. Earnings are due August 4.
content:
Liked this AI Summary?

Shares of Kalyan Jewellers were trading in red as a news report said a prominent domestic mutual fund is likely to offload around 5 crore shares through a block deal.

NDTV Profit reported that the mutual fund is likely to sell shares at a discounted rate of 8-10% without mentioning the name of the mutual fund.

As of June 30, 2026, Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund holds 9.17% stake (around 9.5 crore shares) in the company.

Given the sharp run-up in short time, the mutual fund is looking to sell partial stake. Two bankers have been appointed for the deal, the channel reported.

Kalyan Jewellers shares have risen over 50% in last one month and the company will report its earnings on August 4.

At 11:54 am on July 27,Kalyan Jewellers shareswere trading 1.1% lower at Rs 567 apiece.

The rally in Kalyan Jewellers was triggered after brokerage Citigroup, earlier this month, reiterated its Buy rating on the stock and maintained a target price of Rs 750 per share.

The brokerage had acknowledged that Kalyan Jewellers' June-quarter consolidated revenue growth of 38% year-on-year was below its estimates, but said the softer-than-expected quarter did not alter its constructive long-term view.

Citi expects the company's franchise-led expansion strategy to continue supporting profitable growth while improving return on capital employed (RoCE). It also highlighted the strong momentum in Candere, Kalyan Jewellers' digital-first jewellery business, as a key long-term growth driver.

In its June-quarter business update, Kalyan Jewellers reported 38 percent growth in India revenue, supported by same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 28%. Its international business expanded around 35% year-on-year, with the West Asia operations growing about 30%. International markets contributed roughly 14% of consolidated revenue during the quarter.

Candere remained the standout performer, with revenue surging 112% year-on-year during the quarter. The company also added 12 Kalyan showrooms and five Candere stores, taking its total showroom network to 524 outlets as of June 30. Management said the second quarter had begun on a positive note ahead of the festive and wedding season.

markdown_content:
Liked this AI Summary?

## Market reaction
Shares of Kalyan Jewellers were trading in red after a news report said a prominent domestic mutual fund is likely to offload around 5 crore shares through a block deal. At 11:54 am on July 27, Kalyan Jewellers shares were trading 1.1% lower at Rs 567 apiece.

## Stake sale report
NDTV Profit reported that the mutual fund is likely to sell shares at a discounted rate of 8–10% without mentioning the name of the mutual fund. Given the sharp run-up in a short time, the mutual fund is looking to sell a partial stake. Two bankers have been appointed for the deal, the channel reported.

## Existing holding
* As of June 30, 2026, Motilal Oswal Midcap Fund holds a 9.17% stake (around 9.5 crore shares) in the company.

## Broker view
The rally in Kalyan Jewellers was triggered after brokerage Citigroup, earlier this month, reiterated its “Buy” rating on the stock and maintained a target price of Rs 750 per share. The brokerage acknowledged that Kalyan Jewellers’ June-quarter consolidated revenue growth of 38% year-on-year was below its estimates, but said the softer-than-expected quarter did not alter its constructive long-term view.

Citi expects the company’s franchise-led expansion strategy to continue supporting profitable growth while improving return on capital employed (RoCE). It also highlighted the strong momentum in Candere, Kalyan Jewellers’ digital-first jewellery business, as a key long-term growth driver.

## June-quarter performance and expansion
In its June-quarter business update, Kalyan Jewellers reported:
* 38% growth in India revenue, supported by same-store sales growth (SSSG) of 28%
* International business expansion of around 35% year-on-year, with West Asia operations growing about 30%
* International markets contributed roughly 14% of consolidated revenue during the quarter
* Candere revenue surged 112% year-on-year during the quarter
* The company added 12 Kalyan showrooms and five Candere stores, taking its total showroom network to 524 outlets as of June 30

Management said the second quarter had begun on a positive note ahead of the festive and wedding season.

## Upcoming events
The company will report its earnings on August 4.
